column1: # The hostile bot's engagement policy (eve-bots --hostile --loop hostile;
# eve-bot/src/hostile.rs, CP56; header in docs/content/schema.md §4; plan
# §4.7). Read at eve-bots startup from ./content/bots/hostile.tsv when it is
# there, else this compiled-in copy. Edit and restart the bots.
# - ship_class: the target hull's class: capsule, or the client's rig size
#   (rigSize, 1547) as small, medium, large or capital; * for any hull,
#   including one whose class the bot does not know.
# - min_sec, max_sec: the system's security as the client rounds it,
#   inclusive.
# - engage: 1 attack, 0 leave alone. The FIRST matching row decides; no row
#   matching means leave alone.
# A row can never make the bot commit a crime: wherever crimewatch flags
# apply (security above 0.0 as the client rounds it, or a system the bot has
# no security for) it attacks nobody, whatever this table says (CP3b).
# Every row is [A] as a whole; `why` names what would falsify it.
ship_class
capsule
column5: [A] no podding: falsified by a friend asking the bots to play it rough

column1: small
column5: [A] a Rifter hunts its own size: falsified by friends calling small-ship null roams dull or unfair

column1: medium
column5: [A] a cruiser is a fair fight for a frigate with friends: falsified by bots dying to every cruiser

column1: large
column5: [A] a frigate does not pick a battleship: falsified by a friend wanting a battleship tackled

column1: capital
column5: [A] a frigate does not tackle a capital alone: falsified by a friend wanting one tackled
[A] a hull the bot cannot class is left alone: falsified by bots ignoring shuttles and haulers friends want hunted
